pinned_checkouts_note: Three repositories are pinned here, and only two of them are in `feeds`. `unixnu` and `device_repo` are the two the driver cannot clone for itself (cli.py has no subcommand that clones either; scripts/unixnu/config.py raises 'no device repository' without -D), so the workflow's acquisition step clones them into vendor/. `uefi_sheng` is NOT a feed on purpose: the driver's feeds.fetch() resolves sources named by a feeds.toml and writes them into out/<board>/feeds, and uefi-sheng is named by no feeds.toml -- it is the Mu-Silicium checkout the driver's --uefi option points at (cli.py:24). Adding it to `feeds` would make the workflow's cross-check demand it in the driver's own unixnu.lock, where it will never appear, and would fail every run. So it is pinned here, acquired by the same step, and verified by the one file the build actually reads (uefi_sheng.font_header.sha256) rather than by a feed pin. Measured 2026-10-25: with it absent, build-payload failed on run 40094234507 and 40096928333 with 'Font.h is missing'.

Moved 2026-11-01 from a7b7a03 to ddeb315, one commit on the same fork branch. ddeb315 publishes the console port to native_console_report(), which is what lets the owner-cache mount patch put "system.mount" and "system.volume_identity" on the guest channel. The SystemCryptex mount happens in init's context, long after IOKit matching, so start() cannot report it and native_console_send() cannot either -- it refuses while isOpen(owner) is false and nothing on this board ever opens the port. The port is published only after configure() has allocated both queue buffers, published both rings and set online, and withdrawn under the same IOLock send() takes, so a reporter that read a non-null pointer just before teardown finds online false by the time it gets in. With no live console the entry point returns kIOReturnNotOpen rather than dereferencing null. Note what did NOT catch the need for this: the emitter compiles and links green with the symbol absent, because it is weakly imported and the call site checks for null first -- so the only instrument that can tell the two apart is the wire, which is exactly why the driver commit and the emitter commit are pinned together rather than one at a time. tests/unit/test_native_virtio_console_records.py gains five tests, one per thing the source comment claims, each asserted on the code with comments stripped, and all five mutation-checked. The previous revision's note is kept below. Moved 2026-11-01 from c3c9ce2 to a7b7a03, one commit on the same fork branch, and the reason is a MEASURED defect rather than a plan. The previous pin's three XNU records reached the kernel -- a byte-level grep of the ESP kernel found all five literals, and the ESP kernel's sha256 equalled payload.json's payload_kernel_sha256 -- but only two of them reached the agent channel. The capture is 1224 bytes and ends with the literal bytes  "event"event"event : each XNU record arrived seven bytes long. The cause is in NativeVirtioConsole::start(): the record was selected by a ternary passed straight into the emit macro, NATIVE_CONSOLE_EMIT(NATIVE_CONSOLE_PICK(pt_on,pt_off,mmu_on)), and the two arms are arrays of DIFFERENT lengths -- true is four characters and false is five -- so the conditional operator decays both to char const *. The macro's sizeof(arr) is then the size of a POINTER, 8 on AArch64, and sizeof(arr)-1 is 7. The two IOKit records are sent by name, so they arrived whole, which is exactly why the failure looked selective rather than systemic. The fix selects in an if so every arm names an array, and drops NATIVE_CONSOLE_PICK entirely. Note what did NOT catch this: the build was green under -Werror, and the kernel carries the full literals, so a grep of the image is green too. Only the length argument was wrong and it is computed at run time, so the first instrument that could see it was the wire. tests/unit/test_native_virtio_console_records.py now fails on any length that is not the record's own: it was written first, went red on this defect, and was mutation-checked against three ways of sending a wrong length. The interrupt fact is four static combinations rather than two records because the gate keeps only the FIRST record per event. clang.note: Present on this host as a HOST compiler (x86_64-w64-windows-gnu) AND PROVEN to cross-compile AArch64/iOS. Three independent lines of evidence, all re-run on this host: (1) clang -target arm64-apple-ios17.0 -c emits real Mach-O arm64 objects whose disassembly shows genuine AArch64 instructions, and ld64.lld links a real Mach-O arm64 executable (docs/implementation-plan.md fact 4); (2) docs/kernel-build-windows.md records 61 of 123 osfmk/kern translation units compiled to genuine Mach-O 64-bit arm64 objects, including the 138 KB / 174-symbol osfmk/kern/bsd_kern.c; (3) an 80-line shim plus three -D rewrites for the Apple-clang-only builtins takes that to 79 of 123 with zero regressions. CORRECTION to an earlier note here, which said 'NOT yet proven to cross-compile AArch64/iOS: no iOS sysroot' -- that conflated two different facts. There is indeed no iOS sysroot, and that is still true; but cross-compiling to a Mach-O arm64 object does not require one when the headers are supplied, which is exactly what the freestanding header shim does. The claim of 'not proven' was wrong. What is NOT done is a clean XNU BUILD against these pins -- six build blockers remain (iig, csh/doconf, the five SETUP host tools, ditto/python3 wiring, the Darwin freestanding header set, the Apple-clang builtins; docs/kernel-build-windows.md has the detail), and two required XNU patches are still unapplied in the build tree. availability.pl is present and runs under the host Python (907 lines / 292 macros emitted), so it is not a blocker. mig IS built and working (bootstrap_cmds-138, 73/73 kernel MIG outputs); unifdef and mtools are present in the MSYS2 tree.

unixnu.commit_note:
Moved 2026-11-05 from 1b4f4a7, one commit on the same fork branch, and the whole change is one hunk appended to zzz-native-springboard-events.patch. Addendum AZ concluded from 0 spawn.failed records against 512 spawn.seen that launchd never attempts the SpringBoard spawn. Reading posix_spawn in the XNU source shows that conclusion does not cover the whole function: at kern_exec.c:3869-3880 a caller passing no spawnattr -- or one without POSIX_SPAWN_SETEXEC and no coalition info -- jumps to do_fork1, which FALLS THROUGH to `spawn_no_exec = TRUE` at :4002, and BOTH emitters are inside `if (error == 0 && !spawn_no_exec)`. A spawn on that route emits neither record. So AZ's measurement established "no spawn on the exec path", not "no spawn". The child still execs -- both branches converge on exec_activate_image() at :4250 -- so a child that DIES leaves an exit.seen, and there is none for SpringBoard in any capture; what is left unproven is a child that is ALIVE and blocked, which leaves nothing at all. THE EMITTER closes exactly that hole: `fork1.spawn`, placed at :4250 rather than the `if (spawn_no_exec)` block at :4028 because imgp->ip_vp is assigned at :2255 INSIDE exec_activate_image() and is still NULL at :4028 -- checked, not assumed -- and because p_comm has already been written by set_proc_name() inside exec_mach_imgact(), the same property the spawn.seen emitter 30 lines below depends on and which its 512 correctly-named records prove. It records the image's own name from imgp->ip_vp->v_name, the field kern_exec.c:1294 already uses to name an executable, plus the child's new p_comm, and a one-shot springboard.fork1 so the answer is one grep. ZERO RECORDS IS A REAL ANSWER and a different one from "not measured": the guard is the same XNU_OWNER_CACHE_MOUNT the 512 spawn.seen records prove is live. THE PRE-FLIGHT MATTERS HERE: the hunk's first transcription dropped its opening #if line and **git apply --check accepted the broken hunk**, because git apply verifies context bytes and not C -- so the patch would have applied and failed the kernel link 40 minutes in. Only a compile check caught it, and the added block now compiles clean with -Wall -Werror under both aarch64 targets. The previous revision's note is kept below. Moved 2026-11-05 from 3d83de1, and the whole change is two lines in `.gitmodules` plus the `drivers/NativeMobileDisplay` gitlink: the URL is repointed from UniXNU/NativeMobileDisplay to James081105/GopFramebuffer and the gitlink is moved from eb9c949 to the experiment commit 5b83ab7. Both are required and neither works alone. `apply_divergences` fetches `pin.commit` from the submodule's own origin, and `git submodule update --init --recursive` sets that origin from `.gitmodules` -- so a .gitmodules left on upstream makes a fork commit unfetchable, and a gitlink left at eb9c949 makes `protect()` load-bearing instead of belt-and-braces. This is the same operation performed for drivers/NativeVirtioConsole, recorded in the submodules entry. THE BRANCH MATTERS: this pin lives on fork branch unipad/display-refusal-experiment, not on the fork's main, because the fork's main is upstream's current tip and is ahead of this board's history. The lock does not name the branch anywhere the build reads -- `apply_divergences` fetches by SHA and the SHA is reachable from the branch -- but a reader looking for it should look there, and `git ls-remote` on the fork is how to confirm it. Agent-published: the fork, the branch and both commits were created by Claude Code under the user's standing authorization to develop James081105/unipad. No human reviewed them before they were pushed. The previous revision's note is kept below. Moved 2026-11-04 from ff2f5d1 (the path field).  ONE commit, and it changes
no record's CONTENT -- the same events, the same fields, the same path.  What it
changes is when the emitters stop, and whether they say so.

THE DEFECT.  The six-hour capture on this kernel produced exactly 512 spawn.seen
records and then stopped.  `enum { kMaxSpawnRecords = 512 }` was reached at line
1399 of 1453, and the 54 lines after it are all exits.  Addendum F of interval 47
read that tail as "the loop has not stopped" and "not a throttling failure hidden
by a small sample", both of which are statements about the guest.  Addendum G
retracted them.  The guest did not go quiet; the emitter went blind.

THE EXIT EMITTER'S OWN HEADER PREDICTED IT.  "AND SIXTY-FOUR SATURATED IN
INTERVAL 42.  exit.seen stopped at exactly n=64 ... This is the same defect that
hid 91 of interval 41's 155 spawns on the spawn emitter: that bound went 64 -> 512
afterwards and this one was left behind."  So the cap hid exits at 64, the spawn
cap went 64 -> 512, the exit cap went 64 -> 512 later, and 512 has now saturated
the spawn cap on a six-hour capture.  Three raises of one defect, and the response
has been to move the number each time.

TWO CHANGES, NEITHER OF THEM A BIGGER NUMBER ALONE.

1. Every cap goes 512 -> 65536, and the two 64s with it.  The header's own
   justification for the old values is that "the bound costs four bytes of static
   data", which is an argument for a large bound, not a small one.

2. Each emitter emits ONE record when it reaches its cap, naming the event and
   the source: exec.saturated, exit.saturated, spawn.saturated,
   spawn_failed.saturated, job_open.saturated.  A bounded measurement that stops
   without saying so is indistinguishable from a guest that stopped, and this
   project has now been bitten by exactly that eight times.

ALSO FIXED, FOUND BY COMPILING RATHER THAN READING.  The counter is formatted
into a fixed char buffer and four of the five emitters size it at 4.  65536 needs
five digits.  The digit loop is bounded by sizeof(text), so this is memory-safe,
but it silently drops the leading digit and emits a WRONG n -- 24000 records with
"n":0000 before the fix, 0 after.  Those four buffers go to 8.  The job-open
emitter formats into char digits[12] and needed no change.

AND THE SAME DEFECT CLASS APPEARED AGAIN WHILE BUILDING THIS.  The first version
of the generator wrote the saturation literal's second half without its opening
quote -- an unterminated literal, exactly what revision 2 of the job-open emitter
shipped and what cost a build.  It reached a patch file because every check
applied to it was a text check: brace counts, quote counts, a grep, and the
